chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: My father (peace be upon him) said to me:
No man has hit some part of the Qur'an with another part, except that he has disbelieved.

And I asked Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) about the meaning of this hadith, so he said: It is that you answer a man about the interpretation of one verse with the interpretation of another verse.

key_terms.بَعْضَهُ بِبَعْضٍ: some of it with some of it
key_terms.ضَرَبَ: to strike or hit (metaphorically: to set against or contrast)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'strike' one part of the Qur'an against another?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) defines 'striking one part of the Qur'an with another' as creating internal contradiction by interpreting a verse in a way that negates another, a concept central to Shia hermeneutics. Shaykh al-Saduq’s chain highlights the importance of this distinction, ensuring that the Qur'an is viewed as a coherent whole rather than a collection of disjointed texts. This principle safeguards against *ta'wil* (interpretation) that leads to *kufr* by ignoring the Qur'an's internal consistency.
